"title": "Recurrent Interpolants for Probabilistic Time Series Prediction",
"authors": "Yu Chen, Marin Biloš, Sarthak Mittal, Wei Deng, Kashif Rasul, Anderson Schneider",
"field_subfield": "Machine Learning / Probabilistic Time Series Forecasting",
"type_of_paper": "Method proposal with experimental validation",
"executive_summary": "This paper introduces a novel framework that merges the computational efficiency of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with the high-quality probabilistic modeling of diffusion models, specifically for probabilistic time series forecasting. The authors observe that while autoregressive models such as RNNs and transformers are widely used for capturing sequential dependencies, their probabilistic output layers are confined to simple probability families because the density must be parameterized by neural networks and the loss must be differentiable. To capture more sophisticated distributions and both temporal and cross-feature dependencies, recent works explore generative modeling via diffusion or flow-based models. However, these generative predictors suffer from scalability issues because their model size is related to both feature dimension and the size of the window. The authors propose extending the theory of stochastic interpolants to a more general conditional generation framework with extra control features. Their method relies on the foundation of stochastic interpolants and the extension to a broader conditional generation framework with additional control features, offering insights for future developments. The authors first verify the method on synthetic datasets, then apply it to real-world time series forecasting tasks. On multivariate probabilistic forecasting datasets including Solar, Exchange, Traffic, and Wiki, the proposed stochastic interpolants (SI) method outperforms or matches other models on three out of four datasets, with only the Traffic dataset favoring the flow matching (FM) model. The authors conclude that stochastic interpolants are a strong candidate for conditional generation, in particular for multivariate probabilistic forecasting. The paper's contributions include extending the theory of stochastic interpolants to arbitrary joint distributions and adopting a conditional stochastic interpolants module for sequential modeling and time series prediction. The method is computational-friendly and achieves high-quality modeling of the future time point's distribution. The authors note that their code will be publicly available, though the exact availability is marked with a placeholder in the text. The paper's theoretical contributions are grounded in the extension of stochastic interpolants to arbitrary joint distributions, with the proof being in a spirit similar to prior work but using a continuous-time interpretation. The paper's experimental contributions demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive performance in time series forecasting, with the results for CRPS-sum shown in Table 2 and the results for other metrics consistent with CRPS-sum and shown in Tables 4 and 5 in the appendix. The paper's limitations include the fact that the authors ran a search over flow matching hyperparameters without being able to get satisfying results, and the paper does not provide detailed information about the number of training samples, the specific hyperparameters used, or the computational resources required for training. The paper's future directions include the potential for further research into the application of stochastic interpolants to other time series forecasting tasks and the development of more efficient training algorithms. Overall, the paper makes a significant contribution to the field of probabilistic time series forecasting by proposing a novel framework that combines the strengths of recurrent neural networks and diffusion models, and by demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method on both synthetic and real-world datasets.",

summary.title: Recurrent Interpolants for Probabilistic Time Series Prediction
summary.authors: Yu Chen, Marin Biloš, Sarthak Mittal, Wei Deng, Kashif Rasul, Anderson Schneider
summary.field_subfield: Machine Learning / Probabilistic Time Series Forecasting
summary.executive_summary: This paper proposes a novel probabilistic time series forecasting framework that combines the computational efficiency of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with the high-quality probabilistic modeling of diffusion models, specifically stochastic interpolants (SI). The authors address challenges in modeling high-dimensional complex distributions and cross-feature dependencies that arise with autoregressive and transformer-based models. While these models are widely used in finance, biology, medicine, and other domains, they face scalability issues when applied to large-scale generative model-based predictions. The proposed method extends the theory of stochastic interpolants to a broader conditional generation framework with additional control features, enabling the model to encode long-term temporal dependencies via an RNN while using the generative model to guide future predictions. The framework is trained on tuple data consisting of future, current, and past time points, with importance sampling used to stabilize training. Experiments on synthetic datasets (Circles, Moons, Rings, Swissroll, 8 Gaussians) and real-world datasets (Solar, Exchange, Traffic, Wiki) demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive or superior performance compared to baselines such as DDPM, SGM, FM, and Vec-LSTM. The evaluation uses metrics including CRPS-sum, NRMSE, and ND, with smaller values indicating better performance. The authors conclude that stochastic interpolants are a strong candidate for conditional generation, particularly for multivariate probabilistic forecasting. The paper also highlights the importance of carefully modeling the probability distribution for large-dimensional time series prediction. The code will be publicly available for the camera-ready version, though the exact availability is not yet confirmed. The study contributes to the growing field of generative modeling for time series forecasting by offering a computationally friendly and high-quality approach that advances the application of generative models in this dynamic domain.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper proposes a novel probabilistic time series forecasting framework that combines the computational efficiency of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with the high-quality probabilistic modeling of diffusion models, specifically stochastic interpolants (SI). The authors address challenges in modeling high-dimensional complex distributions and cross-feature dependencies that arise with autoregressive and transformer-based models. While these models are widely used in finance, biology, medicine, and other domains, they face scalability issues when applied to large-scale generative model-based predictions. The proposed method extends the theory of stochastic interpolants to a broader conditional generation framework with additional control features, enabling the model to encode long-term temporal dependencies via an RNN while using the generative model to guide future predictions. The framework is trained on tuple data consisting of future, current, and past time points, with importance sampling used to stabilize training. Experiments on synthetic datasets (Circles, Moons, Rings, Swissroll, 8 Gaussians) and real-world datasets (Solar, Exchange, Traffic, Wiki) demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive or superior performance compared to baselines such as DDPM, SGM, FM, and Vec-LSTM. The evaluation uses metrics including CRPS-sum, NRMSE, and ND, with smaller values indicating better performance. The authors conclude that stochastic interpolants are a strong candidate for conditional generation, particularly for multivariate probabilistic forecasting. The paper also highlights the importance of carefully modeling the probability distribution for large-dimensional time series prediction. The code will be publicly available for the camera-ready version, though the exact availability is not yet confirmed. The study contributes to the growing field of generative modeling for time series forecasting by offering a computationally friendly and high-quality approach that advances the application of generative models in this dynamic domain.

Research Context
Autoregressive and transformer models are the go-to methods for time series forecasting. These models effectively capture short-term and long-term sequential dependencies. Probabilistic forecasting is achieved by incorporating parametric probabilistic models into the output layer. The probabilistic output layer is confined within a simple probability family due to parameterization constraints. Generative modeling via diffusion or flow-based models addresses complex distribution modeling. Recent works have applied diffusion models to probabilistic time series imputation and forecasting. Generative model predictors suffer from scalability issues due to dependence on window size. A computational-friendly framework is needed for large-scale generative model-based predictions. Starting generation from a distribution close to the data distribution alleviates learning challenges. Time series data exhibits strong correlations between neighboring time points.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central research question is whether blending RNN efficiency with diffusion modeling improves probabilistic time series forecasting. The hypothesis is that stochastic interpolants can be extended to a conditional generation framework with extra control features. The hypothesis is that a conditional stochastic interpolants module is computational-friendly and achieves high-quality modeling. The predicted outcome is that the proposed method outperforms or matches baselines on most datasets. The predicted outcome is that stochastic interpolants are a strong candidate for multivariate probabilistic forecasting. The hypothesis is that carefully modeling the probability distribution is critical for large-dimensional time series prediction. The predicted outcome is that the method captures uncertainty even when dimension scales vary significantly.

Methodological Details
The study was conducted by researchers affiliated with Morgan Stanley, Mila, and Université de Montréal. The method relies on the foundation of stochastic interpolants and an extension to a broader conditional generation framework. The training dataset consists of tuples of future, current, and past time points. The context window length is denoted by P, representing the past observations. The generative model learns the joint distribution of the pair (xt+1, xt) given past observations. The marginal distributions are equal because the sample spaces of ρ0 and ρ1 must be the same. An RNN encodes the context window into a history prompt ht for conditional generation. The score function and velocity function perform conditional generation diffusing from xt with the condition input ht. Importance sampling is leveraged to stabilize training by using a Beta distribution for the proposal distribution. The diffusion time si is sampled from a Beta(0.1, 0.1) distribution during training. The loss values become larger when s is close to two ends, motivating the use of importance sampling. The synthetic datasets include Circles, Moons, Rings, Swissroll, and 8 Gaussians. The real-world datasets include Solar, Exchange, Traffic, and Wiki. The probabilistic forecasting is evaluated by CRPS-sum, NRMSE, and ND metrics. The metrics calculation is provided by the gluonts package. All models are assigned to generate data in the same setting by mapping from standard Gaussian to the target distribution. The neural networks and hyperparameters are set the same across models, such as batch size and training epochs. The baseline models include DDPM, SGM, FM, and Vec-LSTM. The preprocessing steps are followed as in [Salinas et al., 2019]. The Solar dataset is used to demonstrate forecast quality on 6 out of 137 variate dimensions.

Procedures And Architectures
The stochastic interpolant constructs a stochastic mapping from t = 0 to t = 1 given values at two ends. The stochastic mapping is characterized by a pair of functions: velocity function b(s, x) and score function s(s, x). The velocity function is defined as the conditional expectation of the derivative of the interpolant. The score function is defined as the gradient of the log marginal density. The velocity and score functions can be modeled by a rich family of functions, such as deep neural networks. The model is trained to match the equality by minimizing the mean squared error loss functions. The forward SDE is used to draw samples from the conditional density ρ(x1|x0) starting from x0 at s = 0. The training algorithm samples si from a Beta distribution and computes loss functions Lb and Ls. The RNN encodes the context into the history prompt ht during inference. The SI transports the context vector xt to the target distribution with the condition ht following the forward SDE. Multiple steps prediction is achieved by recursively running the step-by-step prediction. The modified framework replaces the context time point xt with Gaussian noise for DDPM and SGM-based models. Flow matching fits into the framework by replacing the denoising objective with the flow matching objective. The model diagram is illustrated in Figure 2 for time series prediction. The Time-Grad model is used for conditional time series prediction. The inference algorithm outputs ˜x1 as the prediction of xt+1. The velocity and score functions depend on the condition ξ in the conditional generation framework.

Key Results
The proposed method outperforms or matches other models on three out of four datasets. On the Solar dataset, the SI model achieves a CRPS-sum of 0.359±0.06. On the Exchange dataset, the SI model achieves a CRPS-sum of 0.007±0.001. On the Traffic dataset, the FM model achieves a CRPS-sum of 0.038±0.002, outperforming SI. On the Wiki dataset, the SI model achieves a CRPS-sum of 0.080±0.007. The Vec-LSTM model achieves a CRPS-sum of 0.391±0.017 on the Solar dataset. The DDPM model achieves a CRPS-sum of 0.359±0.061 on the Solar dataset. The SGM model achieves a CRPS-sum of 0.364±0.029 on the Solar dataset. The proposed method captures uncertainty even when the scale of different dimensions varies a lot. The model demonstrates forecast quality on 6 out of 137 variate dimensions. Most gamma-interpolant function combinations achieve good results modeling the target distribution. The Wasserstein distance measures the sample quality between generated samples and true data. All models can capture the true distribution on synthetic datasets. The same holds when using different metrics such as Sliced Wasserstein Distance and Maximum Mean Discrepancy. The SI model achieves a Wasserstein distance of 0.52 for 8 Gaussians with a linear interpolant. The DDPM model with a cosine scheduler achieves a Wasserstein distance of 2.58 for 8 Gaussians. The FM model achieves a Wasserstein distance of 0.58 for 8 Gaussians. The proposed method is a strong candidate for conditional generation, particularly for multivariate probabilistic forecasting. Carefully modeling the probability distribution is critical for large-dimensional time series prediction. On the Wiki data, the FM model cannot capture the data distribution. The proposed method achieves competitive performance in time series forecasting.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The proposed method merges the computational efficiency of RNNs with the high-quality probabilistic modeling of diffusion models. The method is grounded in stochastic interpolants and an expanded conditional generation framework featuring control features. The method advances generative models' application in time series forecasting. The extension of stochastic interpolants to arbitrary joint distributions provides a continuous-time interpretation. The score function is optimized in a simple quadratic objective function. The method offers insights for future developments in this dynamic field. The method provides a computationally friendly framework for large-scale generative model-based predictions. The method addresses challenges in modeling high-dimensional complex distributions and cross-feature dependencies. The method offers a novel approach by blending the computational efficiency of RNNs with the high-quality probabilistic modeling of the diffusion model. Claims

The SI model achieves a CRPS-sum of 0.080±0.007 on the Wiki dataset. On the Traffic dataset, the FM model achieves a CRPS-sum of 0.038±0.002, outperforming SI.
